descriptionChirho: To ride upon an animal, chariot, or (of God) upon the clouds/heavens — the basic intransitive Qal sense covering all finite forms, infinitives, and imperatives.

The Qal active participle used substantivally to denote 'rider' or 'charioteer' — both singular (רֹכֵב) and plural (רֹכְבִים, רֹכְבֵי) construct and absolute forms, including 'the One who rides' as a divine epithet.

labelChirho: Hifil: cause to ride, set upon
descriptionChirho: The Hifil causative meaning 'to cause someone to ride' or 'to mount a person on an animal/chariot' — used when placing or seating a person on a mount, as in enthronement or transport of a dignitary.

A specialized Hifil usage meaning 'to load or place goods/cargo upon an animal for transport' — distinguished from the personal causative by inanimate object, reflected in Korean 실다 (load) and Swahili -pakia (load cargo).
